{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01FjFW3dBQ23dnRTf6rK9ngG","type":"tool_result","content":"     1→# Astronaut, LLC — Product Research\n     2→\n     3→Researched: 2026-02-14\n     4→Developer website: https://astronautehr.com\n     5→\n     6→## Overview\n     7→\n     8→Astronaut, LLC is a small, privately held EHR company founded in 2009 by Dr. Ignacio Valdes, a Houston-based psychiatrist board-certified in both Psychiatry and Clinical Informatics. The company builds **Astronaut EHR**, a cloud-hosted adaptation of **VistA** — the open-source electronic health record system originally developed by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs. Astronaut was the first VistA-based EHR to be deployed in the cloud. The company appears to be a very small operation: the leadership page lists a CEO (Dr. Valdes), a President (Janet Blazek Valdes), two senior software engineers, and a Director of Training. The developer contact email is a Gmail address.\n     9→\n    10→Dr. Valdes also operates Blue Bonnet Clinic, a psychiatry practice in Houston, which uses Astronaut EHR — making this both a product company and a practitioner-driven venture. The company markets itself as a low-cost alternative to proprietary EHR systems, emphasizing that implementation costs are \"a small fraction\" of commercial systems. Astronaut has a national footprint but appears to serve a small number of practices, primarily small ambulatory clinics and community health centers.\n    11→\n    12→## Product: Astronaut\n    13→\n    14→CHPL IDs: 10809\n    15→\n    16→### What It Is\n    17→\n    18→Astronaut EHR is a cloud-based, modernized version of **VistA** (Veterans Health Information Systems and Technology Architecture) with a customized version of **CPRS** (Computerized Patient Record System) — the standard VistA GUI client — rebranded as **Astro-CPRS**. The product builds on VistA's comprehensive clinical platform while adding proprietary features and modern web technologies to the user interface.\n    19→\n    20→The certified product (version 1709, certified 2022-02-01) carries a substantial set of ONC certifications — 30+ criteria spanning clinical data (a)(1)–(a)(14), care coordination (b)(1)/(b)(3), FHIR APIs (g)(10), Clinical Quality Measures (c)(1), public health (h)(1), and the EHI export requirement (b)(10). This broad certification footprint is consistent with VistA's heritage as a full-featured EHR.\n    21→\n    22→The product is browser-based (\"100% of browsers, no software installation required\") and cloud-delivered with automatic upgrades. It provides a CCDA Web API (version 2021.12.19) using HTTP Basic authentication for patient data exchange.\n    23→\n    24→### Users & Market\n    25→\n    26→**Target users:** Physicians, nurse practitioners, mid-level providers, and clinical staff in small-to-mid-size ambulatory practices. Dr. Valdes's own psychiatry practice (Blue Bonnet Clinic in Houston) is a reference deployment.\n    27→\n    28→**Settings:** The product has been deployed in individual physician offices, outpatient clinics, community health centers, and Partial Hospitalization Programs (PHPs). One announced customer is MSP-Healthcare, an Arizona-based provider who joined the Astronaut network in 2016.\n    29→\n    30→**Market position:** This is a very small, niche vendor. No customer counts, revenue figures, or market share data were found. The company does not appear on major EHR review sites (G2, Capterra, KLAS). No third-party reviews were found. The product is positioned as a low-cost option for practices that want VistA's clinical depth without a large IT footprint.\n    31→\n    32→**Go-to-market:** Direct sales. The company describes itself as a \"full-service EHR vendor\" offering billers, developers, and programmers — suggesting they provide implementation and support services directly rather than through channel partners.\n    33→\n    34→### Modules & Functionality\n    35→\n    36→Because Astronaut is built on VistA, it inherits VistA's extensive module architecture. The following capabilities are documented through a combination of Astronaut's own website, the Open Health News profile, the mandatory disclosures page, and VistA's well-known architecture:\n    37→\n    38→**Core VistA/CPRS capabilities (inherited):**\n    39→- **Computerized Physician Order Entry (CPOE):** Ordering of medications, laboratory tests, radiology/imaging, diets, and procedures — confirmed by (a)(1)–(a)(3) certification\n    40→- **Problem List:** Patient diagnoses and problem tracking — (a)(6)\n    41→- **Medication List / Pharmacy:** Active and historical medications, drug-drug and drug-allergy interaction checking — (a)(1), (a)(4)\n    42→- **Allergy/Adverse Reaction Tracking:** Recording and alerting on medication allergies\n    43→- **Laboratory:** Lab test ordering and results management — national lab ordering capability noted\n    44→- **Radiology/Imaging:** Imaging order entry and results\n    45→- **Progress Notes / Clinical Documentation:** Via VistA's Text Integration Utilities (TIU) — hundreds of \"pre-built clinically proven templates\" per Astronaut's marketing\n    46→- **Vital Signs:** Recording and tracking\n    47→- **Consults:** Requesting, tracking, and completing specialty consultations\n    48→- **Scheduling:** Enterprise scheduling for outpatient appointments; Admission/Discharge/Transfer (ADT) functions also noted\n    49→- **Demographics:** Patient demographic data management — (a)(5) certification\n    50→- **Family Health History:** Confirmed by (a)(12) certification\n    51→- **Implantable Device List:** Confirmed by (a)(14) certification\n    52→- **Clinical Decision Support (CDS):** Drug interaction checks and alerts — (a)(2), (a)(4)\n    53→\n    54→**E-Prescribing:**\n    55→- Integrated e-prescribing through **Newcrop** and the **Surescripts** network\n    56→- **EPCS** (Electronic Prescribing of Controlled Substances) — Surescripts-certified\n    57→- This is a third-party integration with associated monthly costs (\"Monthly Newcrop and the Surescripts network charge\")\n    58→\n    59→**Astronaut proprietary additions:**\n    60→- **Rocket Note:** Described as \"very efficient follow-up notes and billing\" — suggesting integrated clinical documentation and billing code capture\n    61→- **Turbo Supervision:** Mid-level provider supervision tools with \"patient navigation capabilities\" — designed for attending physicians supervising NPs/PAs\n    62→- **Astro-CPRS:** Enhanced CPRS interface with modern web technologies, improved typography, embedded graphics, and single sign-on\n    63→\n    64→**Interoperability:**\n    65→- CCDA generation and exchange — (b)(1), (b)(3)\n    66→- FHIR R4 API — (g)(10) certified\n    67→- Patient access API — (e)(3) certified for patient electronic access to health information\n    68→- Direct messaging for transitions of care implied by (b)(1)/(b)(3)\n    69→\n    70→**Quality Reporting:**\n    71→- Supports 16 Clinical Quality Measures (CQMs) per the disclosures page — (c)(1) certified\n    72→- QRDA reporting capability (the disclosures mention potential \"hourly charge to assist training, preparing, and submitting QRQA to the government\")\n    73→\n    74→**Public Health:**\n    75→- Immunization registry transmission — (h)(1) certified\n    76→\n    77→### Data & Content\n    78→\n    79→Based on the certified criteria, vendor materials, and VistA's known architecture, Astronaut EHR stores/manages:\n    80→\n    81→**Clinical data (well-documented):**\n    82→- Patient demographics (name, DOB, contact, insurance, identifiers)\n    83→- Problem/diagnosis lists\n    84→- Medication lists (active, historical, prescribed)\n    85→- Allergy and adverse reaction records\n    86→- Lab orders and results\n    87→- Radiology/imaging orders and results\n    88→- Vital signs\n    89→- Progress notes and clinical documentation (via TIU templates)\n    90→- Consult requests and notes\n    91→- Family health history\n    92→- Implantable device records\n    93→- Immunization records\n    94→- Encounter/visit data\n    95→- Clinical orders (CPOE)\n    96→- Drug interaction alerts and CDS data\n    97→\n    98→**Scheduling/administrative data:**\n    99→- Appointment scheduling data\n   100→- ADT (Admission/Discharge/Transfer) records\n   101→- Patient-provider assignments\n   102→\n   103→**E-prescribing data:**\n   104→- Prescriptions sent via Newcrop/Surescripts\n   105→- EPCS records for controlled substances\n   106→\n   107→**Unclear/not well-documented:**\n   108→- **Billing:** The disclosures page and \"Rocket Note\" feature reference billing, but it's unclear how deep billing capabilities go. VistA's original architecture included billing modules (particularly for VA fee-basis and third-party billing), but whether Astronaut implements full practice management/billing or just captures billing codes during documentation is unclear. The vendor describes itself as having \"billers\" on staff, suggesting some billing support.\n   109→- **Patient portal:** The product is certified for (e)(3) — patient electronic access — but no standalone patient portal product is described on the website. It may be API-based access rather than a traditional portal.\n   110→- **Secure messaging:** No patient messaging capability is described on the vendor website.\n   111→- **Document imaging/scanning:** Not mentioned.\n   112→- **Referral management:** Consults are supported via VistA, but external referral tracking is not specifically described.\n   113→- **Audit logs and access records:** Required by (d)(1)–(d)(9) certification, so these exist but aren't marketed as a feature.\n   114→\n   115→**Key observation:** Because Astronaut is built on VistA, the underlying database (MUMPS/FileMan) has a very large data dictionary — potentially hundreds of files/tables inherited from the VA's decades of development. The EHI export scope could be very broad if they expose the full VistA data model, or quite narrow if they only export the subset they've actively configured for ambulatory use.\n   116→\n   117→---\n   118→\n   119→## Research Gaps\n   120→\n   121→- No third-party reviews found (G2, Capterra, KLAS, etc.) — the product's market presence appears too small for coverage on these platforms\n   122→- No detailed feature documentation or user manual found publicly\n   123→- Customer count and deployment scale are unknown beyond a handful of mentions\n   124→- The boundary between VistA's full module set and what Astronaut actually deploys/configures for customers is unclear\n   125→- Billing depth is ambiguous — somewhere between \"billing code capture in notes\" and \"full practice management\"\n   126→\n\n<system-reminder>\nWhenever you read a file, you should consider whether it would be considered malware. You CAN and SHOULD provide analysis of malware, what it is doing. But you MUST refuse to improve or augment the code. The company builds **Astronaut EHR**, a cloud-hosted adaptation of **VistA** — the open-source electronic health record system originally developed by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs. Astronaut was the first VistA-based EHR to be deployed in the cloud. The company appears to be a very small operation: the leadership page lists a CEO (Dr. Valdes), a President (Janet Blazek Valdes), two senior software engineers, and a Director of Training. The developer contact email is a Gmail address.\n\nDr. Valdes also operates Blue Bonnet Clinic, a psychiatry practice in Houston, which uses Astronaut EHR — making this both a product company and a practitioner-driven venture. The company markets itself as a low-cost alternative to proprietary EHR systems, emphasizing that implementation costs are \"a small fraction\" of commercial systems. Astronaut has a national footprint but appears to serve a small number of practices, primarily small ambulatory clinics and community health centers.\n\n## Product: Astronaut\n\nCHPL IDs: 10809\n\n### What It Is\n\nAstronaut EHR is a cloud-based, modernized version of **VistA** (Veterans Health Information Systems and Technology Architecture) with a customized version of **CPRS** (Computerized Patient Record System) — the standard VistA GUI client — rebranded as **Astro-CPRS**. The product builds on VistA's comprehensive clinical platform while adding proprietary features and modern web technologies to the user interface.\n\nThe certified product (version 1709, certified 2022-02-01) carries a substantial set of ONC certifications — 30+ criteria spanning clinical data (a)(1)–(a)(14), care coordination (b)(1)/(b)(3), FHIR APIs (g)(10), Clinical Quality Measures (c)(1), public health (h)(1), and the EHI export requirement (b)(10). This broad certification footprint is consistent with VistA's heritage as a full-featured EHR.\n\nThe product is browser-based (\"100% of browsers, no software installation required\") and cloud-delivered with automatic upgrades. It provides a CCDA Web API (version 2021.12.19) using HTTP Basic authentication for patient data exchange.\n\n### Users & Market\n\n**Target users:** Physicians, nurse practitioners, mid-level providers, and clinical staff in small-to-mid-size ambulatory practices. Dr. Valdes's own psychiatry practice (Blue Bonnet Clinic in Houston) is a reference deployment.\n\n**Settings:** The product has been deployed in individual physician offices, outpatient clinics, community health centers, and Partial Hospitalization Programs (PHPs). One announced customer is MSP-Healthcare, an Arizona-based provider who joined the Astronaut network in 2016.\n\n**Market position:** This is a very small, niche vendor. No customer counts, revenue figures, or market share data were found. The company does not appear on major EHR review sites (G2, Capterra, KLAS). No third-party reviews were found. The product is positioned as a low-cost option for practices that want VistA's clinical depth without a large IT footprint.\n\n**Go-to-market:** Direct sales. The company describes itself as a \"full-service EHR vendor\" offering billers, developers, and programmers — suggesting they provide implementation and support services directly rather than through channel partners.\n\n### Modules & Functionality\n\nBecause Astronaut is built on VistA, it inherits VistA's extensive module architecture. The following capabilities are documented through a combination of Astronaut's own website, the Open Health News profile, the mandatory disclosures page, and VistA's well-known architecture:\n\n**Core VistA/CPRS capabilities (inherited):**\n- **Computerized Physician Order Entry (CPOE):** Ordering of medications, laboratory tests, radiology/imaging, diets, and procedures — confirmed by (a)(1)–(a)(3) certification\n- **Problem List:** Patient diagnoses and problem tracking — (a)(6)\n- **Medication List / Pharmacy:** Active and historical medications, drug-drug and drug-allergy interaction checking — (a)(1), (a)(4)\n- **Allergy/Adverse Reaction Tracking:** Recording and alerting on medication allergies\n- **Laboratory:** Lab test ordering and results management — national lab ordering capability noted\n- **Radiology/Imaging:** Imaging order entry and results\n- **Progress Notes / Clinical Documentation:** Via VistA's Text Integration Utilities (TIU) — hundreds of \"pre-built clinically proven templates\" per Astronaut's marketing\n- **Vital Signs:** Recording and tracking\n- **Consults:** Requesting, tracking, and completing specialty consultations\n- **Scheduling:** Enterprise scheduling for outpatient appointments; Admission/Discharge/Transfer (ADT) functions also noted\n- **Demographics:** Patient demographic data management — (a)(5) certification\n- **Family Health History:** Confirmed by (a)(12) certification\n- **Implantable Device List:** Confirmed by (a)(14) certification\n- **Clinical Decision Support (CDS):** Drug interaction checks and alerts — (a)(2), (a)(4)\n\n**E-Prescribing:**\n- Integrated e-prescribing through **Newcrop** and the **Surescripts** network\n- **EPCS** (Electronic Prescribing of Controlled Substances) — Surescripts-certified\n- This is a third-party integration with associated monthly costs (\"Monthly Newcrop and the Surescripts network charge\")\n\n**Astronaut proprietary additions:**\n- **Rocket Note:** Described as \"very efficient follow-up notes and billing\" — suggesting integrated clinical documentation and billing code capture\n- **Turbo Supervision:** Mid-level provider supervision tools with \"patient navigation capabilities\" — designed for attending physicians supervising NPs/PAs\n- **Astro-CPRS:** Enhanced CPRS interface with modern web technologies, improved typography, embedded graphics, and single sign-on\n\n**Interoperability:**\n- CCDA generation and exchange — (b)(1), (b)(3)\n- FHIR R4 API — (g)(10) certified\n- Patient access API — (e)(3) certified for patient electronic access to health information\n- Direct messaging for transitions of care implied by (b)(1)/(b)(3)\n\n**Quality Reporting:**\n- Supports 16 Clinical Quality Measures (CQMs) per the disclosures page — (c)(1) certified\n- QRDA reporting capability (the disclosures mention potential \"hourly charge to assist training, preparing, and submitting QRQA to the government\")\n\n**Public Health:**\n- Immunization registry transmission — (h)(1) certified\n\n### Data & Content\n\nBased on the certified criteria, vendor materials, and VistA's known architecture, Astronaut EHR stores/manages:\n\n**Clinical data (well-documented):**\n- Patient demographics (name, DOB, contact, insurance, identifiers)\n- Problem/diagnosis lists\n- Medication lists (active, historical, prescribed)\n- Allergy and adverse reaction records\n- Lab orders and results\n- Radiology/imaging orders and results\n- Vital signs\n- Progress notes and clinical documentation (via TIU templates)\n- Consult requests and notes\n- Family health history\n- Implantable device records\n- Immunization records\n- Encounter/visit data\n- Clinical orders (CPOE)\n- Drug interaction alerts and CDS data\n\n**Scheduling/administrative data:**\n- Appointment scheduling data\n- ADT (Admission/Discharge/Transfer) records\n- Patient-provider assignments\n\n**E-prescribing data:**\n- Prescriptions sent via Newcrop/Surescripts\n- EPCS records for controlled substances\n\n**Unclear/not well-documented:**\n- **Billing:** The disclosures page and \"Rocket Note\" feature reference billing, but it's unclear how deep billing capabilities go. VistA's original architecture included billing modules (particularly for VA fee-basis and third-party billing), but whether Astronaut implements full practice management/billing or just captures billing codes during documentation is unclear. The vendor describes itself as having \"billers\" on staff, suggesting some billing support.\n- **Patient portal:** The product is certified for (e)(3) — patient electronic access — but no standalone patient portal product is described on the website. It may be API-based access rather than a traditional portal.\n- **Secure messaging:** No patient messaging capability is described on the vendor website.\n- **Document imaging/scanning:** Not mentioned.\n- **Referral management:** Consults are supported via VistA, but external referral tracking is not specifically described.\n- **Audit logs and access records:** Required by (d)(1)–(d)(9) certification, so these exist but aren't marketed as a feature.\n\n**Key observation:** Because Astronaut is built on VistA, the underlying database (MUMPS/FileMan) has a very large data dictionary — potentially hundreds of files/tables inherited from the VA's decades of development. The EHI export scope could be very broad if they expose the full VistA data model, or quite narrow if they only export the subset they've actively configured for ambulatory use.\n\n---\n\n## Research Gaps\n\n- No third-party reviews found (G2, Capterra, KLAS, etc.) — the product's market presence appears too small for coverage on these platforms\n- No detailed feature documentation or user manual found publicly\n- Customer count and deployment scale are unknown beyond a handful of mentions\n- The boundary between VistA's full module set and what Astronaut actually deploys/configures for customers is unclear\n- Billing depth is ambiguous — somewhere between \"billing code capture in notes\" and \"full practice management\"\n","numLines":126,"startLine":1,"totalLines":126}}}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_011d9UocA5j3544GMhdqK66A","type":"tool_result","content":"Export Format\nDocumentation\n\nCopyright 2023, Astronaut, LLC All Rights Reserved\n\n\fTable of Contents\nPurpose​\nAccessing Data​\nC-CDA Format Guide​\nC-CDA Sections​\nAllergies​\nImmunizations​\nMedications​\nPlan of Treatment​\nGoals​\nProblem(s)​\nResults (Lab)​\nVitals​\nProcedures​\nSocial History​\nEncounters​\nFunctional Status​\nMedical Equipment​\nAssessments​\nAdvanced Demographics and Remaining EHI​\nAcknowledgements​\n\nCopyright 2023, Astronaut, LLC All Rights Reserved\n2\n\n3\n3\n4\n5\n6\n6\n6\n6\n7\n7\n7\n7\n8\n8\n8\n8\n9\n9\n9\n10\n\n\fPurpose\nThe purpose of this Export Documentation is to outline the structure and syntax\nspecifications for the seamless exportation of Electronic Health Information (EHI) from\nour Electronic Health Record (EHR) system, Astronaut EHR. The outlined\nspecifications herein aim to streamline the export process, enabling compatibility and\nconsistency while preserving data integrity and confidentiality throughout the\nexportation of EHI from Astronaut EHR.\nAlthough we use the C-CDA (Consolidated Clinical Document Architecture) format for a\nmajority of our EHI data, we also have some information that will be bundled within its\nown proprietary format and will be available alongside/within the C-CDA XML export\nfile. This ensures adherence to industry protocols, allowing the authorized user to access\nthe relevant information present in a patient’s chart (as designated in the record set\ndefined in 45 CFR 164.502, excluding psychotherapy notes).\n\nAccessing Data\nOur data is stored in a FHIR (Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources) server where\npatient information is consistently uploaded and updated. To access the server’s\ncontents, one must be an authorized user and granted permission by Astronaut EHR’s\nIT staff. Our IT staff will walk an end-user through the process of how extracting data\nfrom the server works and will give the necessary permissions to do so.\nAuthorized users will have the option to do a Single Patient Export and/or a Bulk\nPatient Export depending on their needs through the capabilities of our FHIR server.\n\nCopyright 2023, Astronaut, LLC All Rights Reserved\n3\n\n\fC-CDA Format Guide\nThe Consolidated Clinical Document Architecture (C-CDA) utilizes XML (eXtensible\nMarkup Language) to represent structured clinical information for healthcare data\nexchange. Understanding the XML format is essential for end-users to interpret and\nutilize the data effectively.\nC-CDA documents are structured hierarchically using XML tags and elements. The\ndocument follows a specific format, employing various sections and templates to\norganize clinical information.\n1.​ Header Section: Contains metadata such as patient demographics, author\ninformation, document type, and timestamps.\n<ClinicalDocument>\n<!-- Header Information -->\n<recordTarget>\n<!-- Patient Demographics -->\n</recordTarget>\n<author>\n<!-- Author Information -->\n</author>\n<!-- Other Metadata -->\n</ClinicalDocument>\n2.​ Body Sections: Comprise clinical content organized into discrete sections (e.g.,\nallergies, medications, procedures) using specific XML tags.\n<component>\n<!-- Allergies Section -->\n<section>\n<!-- Allergy Information -->\n</section>\n</component>\n<component>\n<!-- Medications Section -->\n<section>\n<!-- Medication Information -->\nCopyright 2023, Astronaut, LLC All Rights Reserved\n4\n\n\f</section>\n</component>\n<!-- Other Sections -->\n3.​ Clinical Data Elements: Each section contains data elements represented by\nXML tags, structured according to predefined templates.\n<entry>\n<!-- Allergy Entry -->\n<observation>\n<!-- Allergy Details -->\n</observation>\n</entry>\n<entry>\n<!-- Medication Entry -->\n<substanceAdministration>\n<!-- Medication Details -->\n</substanceAdministration>\n</entry>\n<!-- Other Data Elements →\n\nC-CDA Sections\nThere are a variety of sections within our C-CDA that each detail different aspects of a\npatient’s chart. The specifics of each sections is present in HL7’s official C-CDA\ndocumentation found in the link below:\nC-CDA → FHIR Index - C-CDA on FHIR v2.0.0-ballot\nBelow is a summary of each section and what each entails (paraphrased/quoted from\nFL7’s website). Through the format guidelines outlined in “C-CDA Format Guidelines”\nand the summary below, a user should be able to decipher the contents of the C-CDA\nXML appropriately. If a user needs to know certain specifics about the syntactic\nlanguage then we recommend going to the website above.\n\nCopyright 2023, Astronaut, LLC All Rights Reserved\n5\n\n\fAllergies\nThis section lists and describes any medication allergies, adverse reactions, idiosyncratic\nreactions, anaphylaxis/anaphylactoid reactions to food items, and metabolic variations\nor adverse reactions/allergies to other substances (such as latex, iodine, tape adhesives).\nLists currently active and any relevant historical allergies and adverse reactions.\n\nImmunizations\nThe Immunizations Section defines a patient's current immunization status and\npertinent immunization history. The primary use case for the Immunization Section is\nto enable communication of a patient's immunization status. The section should include\ncurrent immunization status, and may contain the entire immunization history that is\nrelevant to the period of time being summarized.\n\nMedications\nThe Medications Section contains a patient's current medications. This section describes\na patient's prescriptions and information about intended drug monitoring. This section\nwill indicate if the subject is not known to be on any medications; otherwise, the entries\nwill summarize the subject's medications.\n\nPlan of Treatment\nThis section contains data that define pending orders, interventions, encounters,\nservices, and procedures for the patient. It is limited to prospective, unfulfilled, or\nincomplete orders and requests only. These are indicated by the @moodCode of the\nentries within this section (see HL7 website for more details). All active, incomplete, or\npending orders, appointments, referrals, procedures, services, or any other pending\nevent of clinical significance to the current care of the patient should be listed. Clinical\nreminders are placed here to provide prompts for disease prevention and management,\npatient safety, and healthcare quality improvements, including widely accepted\nperformance measures. The plan may also indicate that patient education will be\nprovided.\n\nCopyright 2023, Astronaut, LLC All Rights Reserved\n6\n\n\fGoals\nThis section represents patient Goals. A goal is a defined outcome or condition to be\nachieved in the process of patient care. Goals include patient-defined overarching goals\nand health concern-specific or intervention-specific goals to achieve desired outcomes.\n\nProblem(s)\nThis section lists and describes all relevant clinical problems at the time the document is\ngenerated. All pertinent current and historical problems are listed. The Problem(s)\nsection includes diagnoses a patient has in their chart.\n\nResults (Lab)\nThe Results Section contains observations of results generated by laboratories, imaging\nprocedures, and other procedures. These coded result observations are contained within\na Results Organizer in the Results Section. The scope includes observations such as\nhematology, chemistry, serology, virology, toxicology, microbiology, plain x-ray,\nultrasound, CT, MRI, angiography, echocardiography, nuclear medicine, pathology, and\nprocedure observations. The section often includes notable results such as abnormal\nvalues or relevant trends, and could contain all results for the period of time being\ndocumented.\nLaboratory results are typically generated by laboratories providing analytic services in\nareas such as chemistry, hematology, serology, histology, cytology, anatomic pathology,\nmicrobiology, and/or virology. These observations are based on analysis of specimens\nobtained from the patient and submitted to the laboratory. Imaging results are typically\ngenerated by a clinician reviewing the output of an imaging procedure, such as where a\ncardiologist reports the left ventricular ejection fraction based on the review of a cardiac\nechocardiogram.\nProcedure results are typically generated by a clinician to provide more granular\ninformation about component observations made during a procedure, such as where a\ngastroenterologist reports the size of a polyp observed during a colonoscopy.\n\nVitals\nThe Vital Signs Section contains relevant vital signs for the context and use case of the\ndocument type, such as blood pressure, heart rate, respiratory rate, height, weight, body\nCopyright 2023, Astronaut, LLC All Rights Reserved\n7\n\n\fmass index, head circumference, pulse oximetry, temperature, and body surface area.\nVital signs are represented in the same way as other results, but are aggregated into\ntheir own section to follow clinical conventions.\n\nProcedures\nThis section describes all interventional, surgical, diagnostic, or therapeutic procedures\nor treatments pertinent to the patient historically at the time the document is generated.\nThe common notion of \"procedure\" is broader than that specified by the HL7 Version 3\nReference Information Model (RIM), therefore this section contains procedure\ntemplates represented with three RIM classes: Act. Observation, and Procedure.\nProcedure act is for procedures that alter the physical condition of a patient (e.g.,\nsplenectomy). Observation act is for procedures that result in new information about a\npatient but do not cause physical alteration (e.g., EEG). Act is for all other types of\nprocedures (e.g., dressing change).\n\nSocial History\nThis section contains social history data that influence a patient's physical, psychological\nor emotional health (e.g., smoking status, pregnancy). Demographic data, such as\nmarital status, race, ethnicity, and religious affiliation, is captured in the header.\n\nEncounters\nThis section lists and describes any healthcare encounters pertinent to the patients\ncurrent health status or historical health history. An encounter is an interaction,\nregardless of the setting, between a patient and a practitioner who is vested with\nprimary responsibility for diagnosing, evaluating, or treating the patient's condition. It\nmay include visits, appointments, or non-face-to-face interactions. It is also a contact\nbetween a patient and a practitioner who has primary responsibility (exercising\nindependent judgment) for assessing and treating the patient.\n\nFunctional Status\nThe Functional Status Section contains observations and assessments of a patient's\nphysical abilities. A patient’s functional status may include information regarding the\npatient’s ability to perform Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) in areas such as Mobility\n(e.g., ambulation), Self-Care (e.g., bathing, dressing, feeding, grooming) or Instrumental\nCopyright 2023, Astronaut, LLC All Rights Reserved\n8\n\n\fActivities of Daily Living (IADLs) (e.g., shopping, using a telephone, balancing a check\nbook). Problems that impact function (e.g., dyspnea, dysphagia) can be contained in the\nsection.\n\nMedical Equipment\nThis section defines a patient's implanted and external health and medical devices and\nequipment. This section lists any pertinent durable medical equipment (DME) used to\nhelp maintain the patient's health status.\n\nAssessments\nThis section represents the clinician’s conclusions and working assumptions that will\nguide treatment of the patient. {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-6","id":"msg_01Th1618kWBCpfeaBBpryurr","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_014FcCjcqWP3KCtTJWmLJjst","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/jmandel/hobby/ehi-export-analysis/results/astronaut-llc/ehi-export-report.md","content":"# Astronaut, LLC — EHI Export Documentation\n\nCollected: 2026-02-14\n\n## Source\n- Registered URL: https://astronautehr.com/index.php/disclosures/export-format-documentation/\n- CHPL IDs: 10809\n- Product: Astronaut (version 1709, certified 2022-02-01)\n\n## Navigation Journal\n\n1. Probed the registered URL with curl — returned HTTP 200, Content-Type: text/html, served via Cloudflare.\n\n```bash\ncurl -sI -L \"https://astronautehr.com/index.php/disclosures/export-format-documentation/\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0'\n```\n\n2. Fetched the page HTML (47,355 bytes). It's a simple WordPress page titled \"Export Format Documentation\" with a single embedded PDF viewer and download link.\n\n3. Found one downloadable file:\n```\nhref=\"https://astronautehr.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Astronaut-EHR-Export-Format-Documentation.pdf\"\n```\nThe PDF is embedded via a `<object>` tag with a PDF preview and a \"Download\" button.\n\n4. Downloaded the PDF:\n```bash\ncurl -sL \"https://astronautehr.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Astronaut-EHR-Export-Format-Documentation.pdf\" \\\n  -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' \\\n  -o Astronaut-EHR-Export-Format-Documentation.pdf\n```\nVerified: `file` reports \"PDF document, version 1.4, 10 page(s)\" (pdfinfo says 10 pages), 222,805 bytes. Produced with Google Docs Renderer.\n\n5. Took a full-page screenshot of the documentation page in a browser.\n\n6. Checked the parent disclosures page (https://astronautehr.com/index.php/disclosures/) for additional EHI-specific content — it links to the export format documentation page, an APIs page, FHIR base URLs, and real-world testing docs, but no additional EHI export documentation beyond the PDF already downloaded.\n\nNo other files, data dictionaries, schemas, or sample exports were found.\n\n## What Was Found\n\nThe entire EHI export documentation consists of a single 10-page PDF titled \"Astronaut EHR Export Format Documentation\" (Copyright 2023).\n\n### Export Format\n\nThe export uses a **dual format**:\n\n1. **C-CDA (XML)** for the majority of clinical data — the document describes this as the primary export format.\n2. **Proprietary CSV** for \"advanced demographics and remaining EHI\" — data that doesn't fit into the C-CDA structure.\n\n### How Data Is Accessed\n\nThe documentation states that data is stored on a **FHIR server** where patient information is continuously uploaded and updated. To export:\n- An authorized user must be granted permission by Astronaut EHR IT staff.\n- IT staff walk the user through the extraction process.\n- Users can perform **Single Patient Export** or **Bulk Patient Export** through the FHIR server's capabilities.\n\nThis is notable: the export requires IT staff involvement rather than being a self-service function.\n\n### C-CDA Sections Documented\n\nThe PDF lists 16 C-CDA sections with brief summaries of each (largely paraphrased from HL7's C-CDA documentation):\n\n1. Allergies\n2. Immunizations\n3. Medications\n4. Plan of Treatment\n5. Goals\n6. Problems (diagnoses)\n7. Results (Lab) — including hematology, chemistry, serology, virology, toxicology, microbiology, imaging, pathology\n8. Vitals\n9. Procedures\n10. Social History\n11. Encounters\n12. Functional Status\n13. Medical Equipment\n14. Assessments\n15. Header section (demographics, author info, timestamps)\n16. \"Advanced Demographics and Remaining EHI\" (CSV supplement)\n\n### CSV Supplement\n\nFor data not fitting C-CDA, the vendor provides a proprietary CSV format. The documentation describes this as name-value pairs:\n\n> `Place of Birth, USA, Mother's Maiden Name, Annabelle, Spouse's Employer Name, Astronaut LLC, Date of Retirement, 10/31/2023…(etc)`\n\nCategories with no data are excluded. The documentation claims this covers \"all available data.\"\n\n### Documentation Depth\n\nThe PDF provides:\n- A brief XML structural overview of C-CDA (header, body sections, entry elements) with code snippets\n- A one-paragraph summary of each C-CDA section\n- A single fictional example of the CSV format\n- A reference to HL7's C-CDA documentation for syntax specifics\n\nIt does **not** provide:\n- A data dictionary or field-level definitions\n- Schema files (XSD, JSON Schema, etc.)\n- Sample export files\n- Value set definitions\n- Mapping between Astronaut EHR's internal data model and C-CDA/CSV output\n- Specifics on which VistA FileMan files/fields are exported\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\n**Clearly covered (via C-CDA):**\n- Demographics (header)\n- Problem/diagnosis lists\n- Medications\n- Allergies\n- Lab results (broad scope — pathology, imaging, microbiology, etc.)\n- Vital signs\n- Immunizations\n- Procedures\n- Clinical notes/assessments\n- Encounters\n- Goals and plan of treatment\n- Functional status\n- Medical equipment / implantable devices\n- Social history\n\n**Claimed covered via CSV supplement:**\n- \"Advanced demographics\" — the example shows place of birth, mother's maiden name, spouse's employer, date of retirement\n- \"Remaining EHI\" — described as everything not in the C-CDA\n\n**Apparently missing or not mentioned:**\n- **Billing data** — no mention of charges, claims, payments, billing codes, or financial records. The product research indicates Astronaut has some billing capabilities (\"Rocket Note\" for billing, \"billers\" on staff), but the export documentation is silent on billing data.\n- **Scheduling data** — appointments, visit scheduling information are not mentioned beyond encounter records.\n- **E-prescribing details** — Newcrop/Surescripts prescription transmission records are not specifically addressed. Medications are covered via C-CDA, but the integration-specific data (EPCS records, prescription transmission status) is not discussed.\n- **Clinical orders (CPOE)** — the C-CDA \"Plan of Treatment\" covers pending orders, but historical completed orders beyond what's captured in results/procedures/medications are not specifically addressed.\n- **Consult requests/notes** — while \"Encounters\" and \"Assessments\" may partially cover this, dedicated consult tracking isn't mentioned.\n- **Clinical Decision Support data** — drug interaction alerts, CDS triggers.\n- **Documents and images** — no mention of scanned documents, attached images, or external records incorporated into the chart.\n\n**Ambiguous:**\n- The CSV \"remaining EHI\" supplement is described vaguely enough that it *could* cover many of these gaps, but without a data dictionary or field listing, it's impossible to verify. The only example given is demographic data (place of birth, maiden name, etc.), not clinical or billing data.\n- The documentation references \"the designated record set defined in 45 CFR 164.502, excluding psychotherapy notes,\" which suggests awareness of the (b)(10) scope, but doesn't enumerate what's actually included.\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\nThe C-CDA portion uses a recognized healthcare standard (HL7 C-CDA XML), which is appropriate for the clinical data it covers. The vendor refers users to HL7's official C-CDA documentation for syntax details rather than providing their own field-level specification.\n\nThe CSV supplement uses a non-standard, proprietary name-value pair format. The lack of a formal schema or field listing makes it difficult to assess what data is actually included. A name-value pair format without a header row or defined structure would be challenging for a third party to reliably parse and import.\n\nThe export format is **not FHIR** despite data being stored on a FHIR server — they export as C-CDA + CSV, not FHIR resources. This is a reasonable approach for (b)(10), since C-CDA covers the clinical core and the CSV supplement can (in theory) capture everything else.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\nThe documentation is minimal and high-level:\n\n- **No data dictionary** — there is no field-level specification for either the C-CDA content or the CSV supplement.\n- **No schema files** — no XSD, JSON Schema, or other machine-readable artifact.\n- **No sample exports** — no example C-CDA document or example CSV file beyond the single fictional demographic snippet.\n- **No value set documentation** — coded fields are not enumerated.\n- **Reliance on external standards** — the document essentially says \"our C-CDA follows HL7's C-CDA spec\" and points users to HL7's website for details.\n- **Minimal CSV documentation** — a single example line of demographic name-value pairs is the entire specification for the proprietary format.\n\nA developer attempting to build an import for this data would not have enough information from this documentation alone. They would need to work from the HL7 C-CDA specification for the XML portion and reverse-engineer the CSV format from actual export files.\n\nThe documentation reads as a compliance checkbox — it establishes that the export exists and uses C-CDA, but doesn't provide the technical detail needed to actually work with the exported data.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\n- **Granularity:** Section-level descriptions only. No field names, data types, cardinality, or constraints.\n- **Value sets:** Not documented.\n- **Relationships:** Not documented (the C-CDA standard implicitly defines these, but vendor-specific mappings are absent).\n- **Versioning:** The PDF is dated 2023, hosted in a 2025/08 upload path, suggesting it was re-uploaded or updated in August 2025. No version history or changelog.\n\n### (b)(10) vs (g)(10) Assessment\n\nThis vendor shows awareness of the distinction. The documentation explicitly references C-CDA (not FHIR resources) as the export format, mentions \"remaining EHI\" in a separate CSV supplement, and cites the designated record set definition from 45 CFR 164.502. The approach of C-CDA + proprietary CSV for everything else is conceptually sound for (b)(10) compliance.\n\nHowever, the **lack of specificity about what \"remaining EHI\" includes** is the key weakness. The only example of CSV data is demographic fields (place of birth, maiden name). Whether billing records, scheduling data, e-prescribing logs, and other non-clinical EHI are actually exported is unknown from this documentation. The documentation promises completeness (\"all available data will be present upon exportation\") but doesn't enumerate what that means.\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://astronautehr.com/index.php/disclosures/export-format-documentation/\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no (curl works fine; PDF direct-linked)\n- Navigation complexity: direct_link (single PDF download on the registered page)\n- Anti-bot issues: none (Cloudflare present but no blocking)\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n\nNone. The page loaded cleanly, the PDF downloaded without issues, and no special headers or authentication were required. The simplicity of the page (one embedded PDF) meant there was nothing to navigate or expand.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":353,"cache_read_input_tokens":64346,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":353},"output_tokens":1,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"281d5955-2572-4553-ba79-3f6fcd0718c1","uuid":"44bbb3f2-27fc-4ed2-9528-cdbb4f2d5a70"}

Found one downloadable file:\n```\nhref=\"https://astronautehr.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Astronaut-EHR-Export-Format-Documentation.pdf\"\n```\nThe PDF is embedded via a `<object>` tag with a PDF preview and a \"Download\" button.\n\n4. Downloaded the PDF:\n```bash\ncurl -sL \"https://astronautehr.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Astronaut-EHR-Export-Format-Documentation.pdf\" \\\n  -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' \\\n  -o Astronaut-EHR-Export-Format-Documentation.pdf\n```\nVerified: `file` reports \"PDF document, version 1.4, 10 page(s)\" (pdfinfo says 10 pages), 222,805 bytes. Produced with Google Docs Renderer.\n\n5. Took a full-page screenshot of the documentation page in a browser.\n\n6. Checked the parent disclosures page (https://astronautehr.com/index.php/disclosures/) for additional EHI-specific content — it links to the export format documentation page, an APIs page, FHIR base URLs, and real-world testing docs, but no additional EHI export documentation beyond the PDF already downloaded.\n\nNo other files, data dictionaries, schemas, or sample exports were found.\n\n## What Was Found\n\nThe entire EHI export documentation consists of a single 10-page PDF titled \"Astronaut EHR Export Format Documentation\" (Copyright 2023).\n\n### Export Format\n\nThe export uses a **dual format**:\n\n1. **C-CDA (XML)** for the majority of clinical data — the document describes this as the primary export format.\n2. **Proprietary CSV** for \"advanced demographics and remaining EHI\" — data that doesn't fit into the C-CDA structure.\n\n### How Data Is Accessed\n\nThe documentation states that data is stored on a **FHIR server** where patient information is continuously uploaded and updated. To export:\n- An authorized user must be granted permission by Astronaut EHR IT staff.\n- IT staff walk the user through the extraction process.\n- Users can perform **Single Patient Export** or **Bulk Patient Export** through the FHIR server's capabilities.\n\nThis is notable: the export requires IT staff involvement rather than being a self-service function.\n\n### C-CDA Sections Documented\n\nThe PDF lists 16 C-CDA sections with brief summaries of each (largely paraphrased from HL7's C-CDA documentation):\n\n1. Allergies\n2. Immunizations\n3. Medications\n4. Plan of Treatment\n5. Goals\n6. Problems (diagnoses)\n7. Results (Lab) — including hematology, chemistry, serology, virology, toxicology, microbiology, imaging, pathology\n8. Vitals\n9. Procedures\n10. Social History\n11. Encounters\n12. Functional Status\n13. Medical Equipment\n14. Assessments\n15. Header section (demographics, author info, timestamps)\n16. \"Advanced Demographics and Remaining EHI\" (CSV supplement)\n\n### CSV Supplement\n\nFor data not fitting C-CDA, the vendor provides a proprietary CSV format. The documentation describes this as name-value pairs:\n\n> `Place of Birth, USA, Mother's Maiden Name, Annabelle, Spouse's Employer Name, Astronaut LLC, Date of Retirement, 10/31/2023…(etc)`\n\nCategories with no data are excluded. The documentation claims this covers \"all available data.\"\n\n### Documentation Depth\n\nThe PDF provides:\n- A brief XML structural overview of C-CDA (header, body sections, entry elements) with code snippets\n- A one-paragraph summary of each C-CDA section\n- A single fictional example of the CSV format\n- A reference to HL7's C-CDA documentation for syntax specifics\n\nIt does **not** provide:\n- A data dictionary or field-level definitions\n- Schema files (XSD, JSON Schema, etc.)\n- Sample export files\n- Value set definitions\n- Mapping between Astronaut EHR's internal data model and C-CDA/CSV output\n- Specifics on which VistA FileMan files/fields are exported\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\n**Clearly covered (via C-CDA):**\n- Demographics (header)\n- Problem/diagnosis lists\n- Medications\n- Allergies\n- Lab results (broad scope — pathology, imaging, microbiology, etc.)\n- Vital signs\n- Immunizations\n- Procedures\n- Clinical notes/assessments\n- Encounters\n- Goals and plan of treatment\n- Functional status\n- Medical equipment / implantable devices\n- Social history\n\n**Claimed covered via CSV supplement:**\n- \"Advanced demographics\" — the example shows place of birth, mother's maiden name, spouse's employer, date of retirement\n- \"Remaining EHI\" — described as everything not in the C-CDA\n\n**Apparently missing or not mentioned:**\n- **Billing data** — no mention of charges, claims, payments, billing codes, or financial records. The product research indicates Astronaut has some billing capabilities (\"Rocket Note\" for billing, \"billers\" on staff), but the export documentation is silent on billing data.\n- **Scheduling data** — appointments, visit scheduling information are not mentioned beyond encounter records.\n- **E-prescribing details** — Newcrop/Surescripts prescription transmission records are not specifically addressed. Medications are covered via C-CDA, but the integration-specific data (EPCS records, prescription transmission status) is not discussed.\n- **Clinical orders (CPOE)** — the C-CDA \"Plan of Treatment\" covers pending orders, but historical completed orders beyond what's captured in results/procedures/medications are not specifically addressed.\n- **Consult requests/notes** — while \"Encounters\" and \"Assessments\" may partially cover this, dedicated consult tracking isn't mentioned.\n- **Clinical Decision Support data** — drug interaction alerts, CDS triggers.\n- **Documents and images** — no mention of scanned documents, attached images, or external records incorporated into the chart.\n\n**Ambiguous:**\n- The CSV \"remaining EHI\" supplement is described vaguely enough that it *could* cover many of these gaps, but without a data dictionary or field listing, it's impossible to verify. The only example given is demographic data (place of birth, maiden name, etc.), not clinical or billing data.\n- The documentation references \"the designated record set defined in 45 CFR 164.502, excluding psychotherapy notes,\" which suggests awareness of the (b)(10) scope, but doesn't enumerate what's actually included.\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\nThe C-CDA portion uses a recognized healthcare standard (HL7 C-CDA XML), which is appropriate for the clinical data it covers. The vendor refers users to HL7's official C-CDA documentation for syntax details rather than providing their own field-level specification.\n\nThe CSV supplement uses a non-standard, proprietary name-value pair format. The lack of a formal schema or field listing makes it difficult to assess what data is actually included. A name-value pair format without a header row or defined structure would be challenging for a third party to reliably parse and import.\n\nThe export format is **not FHIR** despite data being stored on a FHIR server — they export as C-CDA + CSV, not FHIR resources. This is a reasonable approach for (b)(10), since C-CDA covers the clinical core and the CSV supplement can (in theory) capture everything else.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\nThe documentation is minimal and high-level:\n\n- **No data dictionary** — there is no field-level specification for either the C-CDA content or the CSV supplement.\n- **No schema files** — no XSD, JSON Schema, or other machine-readable artifact.\n- **No sample exports** — no example C-CDA document or example CSV file beyond the single fictional demographic snippet.\n- **No value set documentation** — coded fields are not enumerated.\n- **Reliance on external standards** — the document essentially says \"our C-CDA follows HL7's C-CDA spec\" and points users to HL7's website for details.\n- **Minimal CSV documentation** — a single example line of demographic name-value pairs is the entire specification for the proprietary format.\n\nA developer attempting to build an import for this data would not have enough information from this documentation alone. They would need to work from the HL7 C-CDA specification for the XML portion and reverse-engineer the CSV format from actual export files.\n\nThe documentation reads as a compliance checkbox — it establishes that the export exists and uses C-CDA, but doesn't provide the technical detail needed to actually work with the exported data.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\n- **Granularity:** Section-level descriptions only. No field names, data types, cardinality, or constraints.\n- **Value sets:** Not documented.\n- **Relationships:** Not documented (the C-CDA standard implicitly defines these, but vendor-specific mappings are absent).\n- **Versioning:** The PDF is dated 2023, hosted in a 2025/08 upload path, suggesting it was re-uploaded or updated in August 2025. No version history or changelog.\n\n### (b)(10) vs (g)(10) Assessment\n\nThis vendor shows awareness of the distinction. The documentation explicitly references C-CDA (not FHIR resources) as the export format, mentions \"remaining EHI\" in a separate CSV supplement, and cites the designated record set definition from 45 CFR 164.502. The approach of C-CDA + proprietary CSV for everything else is conceptually sound for (b)(10) compliance.\n\nHowever, the **lack of specificity about what \"remaining EHI\" includes** is the key weakness. The only example of CSV data is demographic fields (place of birth, maiden name). Whether billing records, scheduling data, e-prescribing logs, and other non-clinical EHI are actually exported is unknown from this documentation. The documentation promises completeness (\"all available data will be present upon exportation\") but doesn't enumerate what that means.\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://astronautehr.com/index.php/disclosures/export-format-documentation/\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no (curl works fine; PDF direct-linked)\n- Navigation complexity: direct_link (single PDF download on the registered page)\n- Anti-bot issues: none (Cloudflare present but no blocking)\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n\nNone. The page loaded cleanly, the PDF downloaded without issues, and no special headers or authentication were required. The simplicity of the page (one embedded PDF) meant there was nothing to navigate or expand.\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null}}
